I am all over this game like a Hobo on a Ham Sandwich!

Looks cool. I've seen other attempts at FPS roguelikes but they had orthogonal (90degree) views only.

One of the problems with roguelikes is how to translate the surrounding view to 3D. On roguelike dev forums there is all sorts of insane ideas on how to selectively turn on/off dungeon parts and creatures with culling, draw distance, etc. I've always advocated for vertex fog... This game doesn't seem to care about limiting view distance.

The other things that don't translate to 3D well is the situational awareness of a map view, randomized item effect / identification subgame, and being able to take minutes or hours between moves (turnbased). There's just something about relaxing while minmaxing...

Since the roguelike craze hit Nippon I've seen rogue-lite minigames springing up even in AAA games like Final Fantasy. They all gloss over so many things that make a game like Rogue it's hard to call them Rogue-like at all, more like "inspired somewhat by Rogue or other games that claim to be 'roguelike' but aren't" (hence: rogue-lite).

I'm eager to see how much like rogue the gameplay actually is. I won't get my hopes up though. It could just be yet another 3D dungeon crawler (now with procedural generation!) fallaciously using the "Roguelike" label to generate interest.
